claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 17 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in approved education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or an equivalent qualification) or training (such as certain unpaid, employer-provided training)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is. He's studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you. Studying for A-levels at a sixth form college counts as approved education, which is good for eligibility.

Now, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does he live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you. That's helpful to know.

Just a couple more questions:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one more question to confirm:

Is Alex currently working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He does work quite a bit actually - he has a part-time job at the supermarket and works full-time hours alongside his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. When you say he works "full-time hours," could you tell me approximately how many hours per week Alex works at the supermarket? Specifically, is it 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's more than 24 hours a week. He works quite a lot - fits it in around his college schedule.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Unfortunately, this affects Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit.

Even though Alex is in approved education (studying A-levels), the rules state that Child Benefit stops if a child works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment, even if they're still in approved education or training.

Let me provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not currently eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Although Alex meets several of the usual criteria:
- ✅ You live in the UK
- ✅ Alex lives with you
- ✅ He's under 20 and in approved education (A-levels)

Unfortunately, the rules state that **Child Benefit stops if a child works 24 hours or more per week in paid employment**, even if they're still in approved education or training. Since Alex works more than 24 hours per week at the supermarket, this means you cannot claim Child Benefit for him.

**What this means going forward:**

If Alex's work hours were to reduce to below 24 hours per week while he continues his A-level studies, you may become eligible again. Should his circumstances change, you could consider making a new claim at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like me to clarify?

Since Alex works more than 24 hours per week at a supermarket alongside his studies, this disqualifies him from Child Benefit eligibility.
